news.title: First World Cup win for transplant football team
news.lede: Daley Cross (left) managed the team to success, while Kevin Kyley played up front. England's transplant football team are world champions for the first time. They thrashed Spain 5-1 on Friday to take the crown in Frankfurt, Germany, taking revenge after the country knocked them out at the previous World Cup in 2024. Manager Daley Cross, from Bicester, Oxfordshire, said he could sense that his team were determined to bring the trophy home from the outset.

news.title: Italy football hopes for new dawn under returning Mancini
news.lede: Roberto Mancini, the architect of Italy’s last major triumph at Euro 2020, is back as head coach. ROME – After months of soul-searching, controversy and debate, Italy are ready to let football do the talking again as Roberto Mancini kickstarts his second spell in charge. On Sept 25, the Azzurri begin their UEFA Nations League campaign against Belgium at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome. It will be Italy’s first competitive match since a play-off defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March sealed a humbling third consecutive failure to reach the World Cup.

news.title: World Cup 'not enough' as Spain begin next chapter
news.lede: Spain coach Luis de la Fuente will not allow the World Cup winners to rest on their laurels as they get back into action this week for the first time since their triumph.La Roja may have conquered Europe in 2024 and then the world this summer, but when they face England in the Nations League on Saturday, they will be seeking to improve.De la Fuente said in the aftermath of the World Cup final victory over Argentina in New Jersey in July, he was already looking to the future.The 65-year-old signed a contract extension, keeping him with the team until 2032, earlier this week." In the heat of the moment, two or three minutes later, a player came up to me and said, 'What do we still have to win?' Well, the match against England on September 26th," said De la Fuente." The World Cup isn't enough we have to be better.

news.title: Every Member Federation represented in Australia’s inaugural U-15 National Select squad
news.lede: The 14-player squad features representation from across the country, with players currently based in New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria, Northern New South Wales, Tasmania, the ACT, Northern Territory, South Australia and Western Australia. The selection marks another milestone for Football Australia’s newly established U-15 program, providing some of the country’s emerging young players with their first opportunity to experience international tournament football and a national-team environment. The squad comprises players from a mix of metropolitan and regional environments, reflecting the breadth of Football Australia’s talent identification network and the role of Member Federations, clubs and programs across the country in developing young players.

news.title: Will anyone topple Infantino? How Fifa president is trying to cling on after World Cup sell-off debacle
news.lede: Fifa president continues to lobby for re-election despite no other candidates coming forward to challenge him. For Gianni Infantino there is no international break. The Fifa president is widely expected to make an appearance at the United Nations general assembly this week in New York, where he will lobby heads of state for their federations’ support as he continues his campaign to be re-elected next year. Infantino has not been idle during the lull since Fifa abandoned its World Cup sell-off plan last month, instead crisscrossing the globe on a private jet provided by Qatar Airways as part of its sponsorship deal with world football’s governing body.

news.title: This college football team just adopted Norway's World Cup Viking Row — keeping the viral tradition alive
news.lede: Norway's Viking Row was one of the most viral fan traditions of the 2026 World Cup. Now, two months later, it has officially made its way into American college football. The University of Minnesota debuted its own version of the synchronized rowing chant at its season opener at Huntington Bank Stadium, with the student section sitting in rows and mimicking the same exaggerated rowing motion that Norwegian fans made famous this summer. Former Gophers linebacker Kamal Martin led the chant before kickoff, keeping one of the World Cup's biggest fan traditions going long after the tournament ended.
